items.title: Dorothy Tait Interview, 1968-12-21
items.q: You see a boy like young Tom Sancton, who played at George's Wake, playing this incredibly beautiful George Lewis style clarinet.

ctx.x: Um, how do you feel about the future of this music in general? I mean, as we know in New Orleans, the younger, younger people in New Orleans really aren't thinking out of music. Um, how do you feel about the future in general? Not necessarily for the rest of it.

Mixed, mixed feelings, Tom. Uh, I think it's such a specialized art form it can get away from you unless you hear it and play it as often as possible. I think the tendency, there is, in any band, there's a tendency for a band to disintegrate, less ensemble and more solo. Uh, all over the world, really largely through George, uh, and the recordings, uh, young bands are playing New Orleans style. How deeply rooted this is, I don't know. You see, it isn't this present generation. It isn't the men between 40 and 50…
And we might say here that, uh, Tom Sancton is from New Orleans, which is quite unusual.
